scores.evidence: Phase 0 skeleton includes CRDT merge, offline catch-up and persistence; auth/sharing deferred to Phase 2 while Phase 1 sits on URL tokens
scores.rationale: Mostly substrate-upward with a dependency map, but the skeleton bundles catch-up and CRDT before the merge is proven (V1 is in Phase 1), and the spike exception sits awkwardly before Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: user types a character, server applies to CRDT, broadcasts, persists to PostgreSQL; server restarts and reconstructs text; deploy, rollback, metrics.
scores.rationale: A real end-to-end slice is deployed with logging, monitoring, rollback and an exit check before features.

scores.evidence: CRDT vs OT: Default CRDT (Yjs or Automerge)... Flip condition: V1 fails: switch to an OT library... re-scope to turn-taking locking
scores.rationale: The gate table lists irreversible decisions with reversibility, default, assumption, validation and flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 tasks: CRDT layer, version vectors, protocol, operation log, catchup... then snapshot, purge, load test
scores.rationale: The ordering is roughly sensible (CRDT and schema first) but blast radius is never explicitly used, and the load test and purge are not ordered by impact.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: internal IP allow-list, feature flag off; Phase 1: input validation; Phase 2: auth; Phase 3: rate limiting; Phase 4: CSP
scores.rationale: Each phase has concrete security measures, starting from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Structured JSON logs to stdout; baseline latency metrics to Prometheus; Phase 1 correlation IDs; Phase 2 SLIs and alerts; Phase 3 tracing
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in every phase after.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Docker image build is reproducible (pinned base image, dependencies); database schema is version-controlled
scores.rationale: Each phase has concrete reproducibility items, such as pinned images, versioned migrations, expand/contract migrations, runbooks and release playbooks.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM, flush pending edits to database; Phase 1 circuit breaker; Phase 2 client auto-retry; Phase 3 failover
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears concretely in all phases, including Phase 0.

scores.evidence: N/A — no AI component. The system does not use large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, or agent orchestration.
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A.

scores.evidence: Offline editing... pulled forward if product feedback shows users need it.
scores.rationale: The deferred list is explicit and each item has a pull-forward condition.

note: Strong, well-threaded plan with real skeleton and gates. Weak spots: Phase 0 overloaded before CRDT proof, blast-radius ordering implicit, and some internal inconsistencies.
